page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with a single thread per core configuration. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 133 Gbps. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the c8gb.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core CPU performance and top-tier memory bandwidth, with uncached large block read speeds reaching 466.21 GB/sec and write speeds at 210.01 GB/sec. It excels in memory-bound and parallel processing tasks, scoring in the top tier for Geekbench multi-core performance, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark database operations. Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput also rank in the top tier. However, single-core performance and small-model text generation show relatively lower efficiency, representing a tradeoff for workloads requiring high single-threaded clock speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture delivers high compute density and memory throughput per resource unit compared to traditional x86 alternatives. This makes the instance highly suitable for multi-threaded, compute-intensive workloads. Recommended applications include software compilation, high-throughput static web serving, database operations, parallel data processing, and medium-to-large scale LLM text generation.
